subject: Object property
notes: kb/Work PB1275 LANDED (w1014u). cite.py --check 8.4.3.9.3 'If the object property is used as a sending item, a get property method shall exist' OK 3). The refuted over-application is fixed: STRING's identifier-3 is classified WRITE-only (14.9.43.3 SR10 'The data item referenced by identifier-3 is the receiving operand'), so a WITH NO GET property as the STRING INTO target no longer demands a GET - it compiles and its SET stores the transferred characters (golden line 8, ABCDEFGH); identifier-4 (POINTER) stays read-modify-write. Every true sending use without a GET still raises COBOL0843 naming SR3 (OoSpineTests.PropertyReference_SendingWithNoGet_0843). retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/ReferenceResolver.cs#OoTryBindPropertyReference (the one-word property binder ReferenceResolver.OoTryBindPropertyReference is deleted by kb/Work PB1425 (w1021a): a property reference is resolved by ReferenceResolver.ResolveObjectProperty, which splits the chain and resolves identifier-3 through the ordinary resolver)
